title: Post-test analysis template — Controlled regional failover
content:
Purpose
Use this template after *any* controlled failover test (staging or production) to capture a clear, auditable record of:
- what we intended to test
- what actually happened (timeline)
- customer/platform impact (SLO + error budget view)
- trigger + automation behavior (including manual overrides)
- alerting quality (signal vs noise)
- gaps + follow-ups (owners + due dates)

This document is written for: SRE on-call, Platform/Routing, Infra/Networking, Release Eng, and leadership review.

---

0) Header / metadata
- Test name: [e.g., 2025-05-07 Prod controlled failover — Hosted API low-risk slice]
- Environment: [staging | production]
- Primary region impacted (source): [us-east-1 | eu-west-1 | …]
- Target failover region(s): [us-west-2 | eu-central-1 | …]
- Date/time window (local + UTC): [start/end]
- Change ticket(s): [link]
- Linear parent: [ENG-2850 / ENG-2851]
- Feature flags involved:
  - trigger engine: [flag name + state]
  - orchestrator automation: [flag name + state]
  - progressive failover: [flag name + state]
  - graceful degradation controls: [flag name + state]
- Routing scope:
  - product surface: [Hosted API | Dedicated | Private]
  - customer tiers: [free | pro | enterprise]
  - route/model scope: [list]
  - % traffic / canary strategy: [plan]

Roles
- Incident Commander (IC): [name]
- Comms lead: [name]
- Primary observer (routing/trigger): [name]
- Infra/capacity observer: [name]
- SLO/alerts observer: [name]
- Approval / go-no-go: [name(s)]

---

1) Executive summary (fill last)
Write this *after* the timeline is complete.

- Outcome: [PASS | PASS w/ issues | FAIL]
- What we validated:
  - [ ] trigger detection fired within expected window
  - [ ] safe-to-failover checks prevented unsafe cutover
  - [ ] progressive failover executed in steps and could rollback
  - [ ] graceful degradation maintained “degraded but available” behavior
  - [ ] observability + audit trail usable during live execution
- Customer impact summary:
  - affected surface: [hosted/dedicated/private]
  - visible symptoms: [elevated latency, 5xx, streaming disconnects, etc]
  - estimated affected requests: [# / %]
  - SLO / error budget impact: [high-level numbers]
- Top 3 issues/gaps:
  1) …
  2) …
  3) …
- Decision: [ship/tune/expand scope/hold]

---

2) Hypotheses + success criteria (copy from game day plan, then annotate)
Hypotheses
- H1: [e.g., sustained elevated p99 latency + 5xx in region triggers “DEGRADED” within X minutes]
- H2: [e.g., safe-to-failover blocks cutover if target region headroom < Y]
- H3: [e.g., progressive failover can shift 5% → 25% → 50% → 100% without flapping]

Success criteria (quantitative)
- Detection time: T_detect <= [X min]
- Decision time (automation / IC approval): T_decide <= [Y min]
- Time-to-mitigate (traffic moved or shed): T_mitigate <= [Z min]
- No flapping: <= [N] state transitions in [window]
- Stop conditions never breached (see Section 4)
- Error budget burn: [max allowed burn] during window
- Any customer impact within agreed bounds for the blast radius

Success criteria (qualitative)
- On-call could follow runbook without ambiguity
- Dashboards were sufficient to answer go/no-go questions
- Audit log clearly explains “why” a state transition happened

---

3) Test plan recap (what we actually did)
Planned scenario
- Impairment type: [partial outage | elevated 5xx | network partition | dependency failure | capacity saturation]
- Injection method:
  - [ ] synthetic probe manipulation
  - [ ] fault injection tooling
  - [ ] config-based routing impairment
  - [ ] dependency throttling
  - details: [how]

What changed from plan (if any)
- [explain deltas and why]

---

4) Guardrails + stop conditions (must be explicit)
Stop conditions (if any met → pause/rollback/abort)
- Availability (global): [threshold + window]
- Tail latency (p99/p999): [threshold + window]
- Elevated 5xx: [threshold + window]
- Queue depth / time-in-queue: [threshold]
- Target region headroom: [min GPU headroom, max utilization]
- Dependency health: [specific dependencies + threshold]
- Customer escalation: [e.g., any enterprise escalation from named accounts triggers pause]

What happened
- Were any stop conditions hit? [yes/no]
- If yes: which ones, when, what action taken

---

5) Timeline (authoritative record)
Instructions:
- Capture all times in UTC.
- Prefer linking to exact audit log entries / deploy SHAs / routing policy versions.
- For each row, include “Evidence” links (dashboard screenshot, log query, orchestrator audit event).

Timeline table
| Time (UTC) | Actor/System | Event | Expected? (Y/N) | Observed impact | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [HH:MM:SS] | [system] | [impairment injection started] | Y | [none/latency up] | [link] |
| … | … | … | … | … | … |

Key durations (fill)
- T0 = impairment start: [time]
- T_detect = first trigger condition met: [time] (Δ from T0 = …)
- T_alert = first page (if any): [time] (Δ from T0 = …)
- T_state = orchestrator state change(s): [list with times]
- T_route = first traffic shift observed: [time]
- T_stable = new steady state (no large errors): [time]
- T_recover = end of test / rollback complete: [time]

---

6) Trigger engine behavior (signals → evaluation → decision)
Trigger configuration snapshot
- Trigger(s) enabled: [list]
- Thresholds + windows:
  - error rate: [e.g., 5xx > X% for Y min]
  - tail latency: [p99 > X ms for Y min]
  - dependency: [name + threshold]
  - network probes: [packet loss / RTT threshold]
- Hysteresis / hold-down timers:
  - degrade → failover: [rules]
  - failover → recover: [rules]
  - minimum time in state: [value]

Observed evaluation details
- Which signals fired first? [list]
- Any missing/late signals? [list]
- Any signal that was noisy/false positive? [list]
- Did trigger engine reach the expected state?
  - expected: [DEGRADED → FAILOVER_CANDIDATE → FAILING_OVER → FAILED_OVER]
  - observed: [actual path]

Notes / evidence
- Audit trail link(s): [orchestrator event id(s)]
- Raw metrics queries used to validate: [paste queries]

---

7) Orchestration + routing behavior (state machine + progressive failover)
Routing policy changes executed
- Mechanism(s):
  - [ ] internal routing policy store update
  - [ ] edge/DNS change
  - [ ] both
- Progressive failover steps:
  - Step 0: [monitor-only / 0%]
  - Step 1: [5%] scope: [tier/route/model]
  - Step 2: [25%] scope: …
  - Step 3: [50%] scope: …
  - Step 4: [100%] scope: …

Observed routing outcomes
- Did traffic shift match planned %? [yes/no; details]
- Any “sticky” traffic that didn’t move? [by customer/route?]
- Any evidence of flapping or partial rollback? [details]
- TTL / propagation notes (if DNS involved):
  - planned TTL: [value]
  - observed propagation: [value]
  - surprises: [cache behavior]

Rollback
- Was rollback tested? [yes/no]
- Rollback time: [duration]
- Any residual issues after rollback? [yes/no]

---

8) Safe-to-failover checks (capacity/dependency gating)
Target region readiness snapshot (at decision time)
- GPU headroom / utilization: [numbers]
- Queue depth / scheduling delay: [numbers]
- Error rate + tail latency in target region: [numbers]
- Key dependencies health (target region):
  - dependency A: [healthy/degraded]
  - dependency B: …

Outcomes
- Did gating allow failover? [yes/no]
- If blocked: what specifically failed, and was it correct?
- Any mismatch between “authoritative” capacity signals and what we saw in practice?

---

9) Customer impact analysis (what users experienced)
Define scope (must be consistent with blast radius)
- Customer tiers affected: [list]
- Affected products: [Hosted API / Dedicated]
- Affected endpoints: [chat/completions/embeddings/etc]
- Affected models: [list]

Symptoms observed
- Elevated 5xx: [peak %, duration]
- Elevated timeouts: [peak %, duration]
- Tail latency increase: [p95/p99 deltas]
- Streaming disconnects: [rate]
- Any data correctness issues (should be “none”): [yes/no]

Quantify (fill with numbers; estimate if needed, but label)
- Total requests in scope during window: [#]
- Failed requests attributable to test: [#] ([%])
- Requests with latency > SLO attributable to test: [#] ([%])
- Top impacted customers (if any; avoid listing if not necessary—reference internal IDs): [list or “none”]

Customer comms (if production)
- Status page posted? [yes/no + link]
- Support macros used? [yes/no]
- Any customer escalations? [SUP ticket links]

---

10) SLO + error budget impact
SLOs referenced
- Availability SLO: [name/link]
- Latency SLO: [name/link]

Error budget view (fill)
- Availability burn (test window): [value]
- Availability burn (24h rolling): [value]
- Latency burn (test window): [value]
- Did burn-rate alerts trigger? [yes/no]
- If triggered: were they expected/desired? [yes/no]

Interpretation
- Was impact within pre-approved bounds? [yes/no]
- If no: why (signal thresholds too lax, rollout too aggressive, propagation delays, etc.)

---

11) Alerting behavior (signal vs noise)
Alert inventory (paste from runbook/dashboard)
| Alert name | Condition | Fired? (Y/N) | Time | Was it actionable? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [multi-region availability burn] | … | … | … | … | … |
| [region health degraded] | … | … | … | … | … |

Paging / notification quality
- Did the first page happen too early / too late / correct? [comment]
- Did we get duplicate pages for the same underlying event? [list]
- Any missing pages (should have fired but didn’t)? [list]
- Any noisy pages (should not fire in controlled test)? [list]

Suggested alert changes
- [ ] threshold change
- [ ] window change
- [ ] add/remove dependency signal
- [ ] route alerts to non-paging channel during controlled tests (if policy permits)
- [ ] add annotation/event to dashboards on state transitions

---

12) Observability + debugging notes
Dashboards used (links)
- Region health overview: [link]
- Failover state transitions: [link]
- Customer impact by tier/route/model: [link]
- Capacity headroom: [link]

Logs/traces used
- Orchestrator audit log query: [paste]
- Trigger evaluation debug logs: [paste]
- Routing policy diff/version used: [paste]

What was hard to answer in the moment?
- [question → missing data]

Instrumentation gaps
- Metric missing: [name]
- Cardinality issue: [metric labels too high/low]
- Sampling too low/high: [details]

---

13) What went well / what didn’t (retro-style)
What went well
- …

What didn’t go well
- …

Where we got lucky (optional but encouraged)
- …

---

14) Root causes (if unexpected behavior occurred)
Only fill if there were deviations or failures.

Deviation #1: [title]
- Expected: …
- Observed: …
- Most likely cause: …
- Evidence: …

Deviation #2: …

---

15) Follow-up actions (make this the source of truth)
Instructions:
- Every action must have a single owner and a due date.
- If it’s engineering work, create a Linear issue and link it.
- Tag actions as: [P0 before next prod test] [P1 before expansion] [P2 backlog].

Actions table
| Priority | Action | Owner | Due date | Tracking link | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | [e.g., tune latency trigger threshold from X→Y; add hysteresis] | [name] | [YYYY-MM-DD] | [Linear link] | … |
| P0 | [e.g., add dashboard panel for target region headroom at decision time] | [name] | … | … | … |
| P1 | … | … | … | … | … |

Runbook/doc updates required
- [ ] Automated region failover runbook update
- [ ] Game day plan update
- [ ] Comms template update
- [ ] On-call training / walkthrough schedule

---

16) Appendix
A) Config snapshot
- Trigger config YAML/JSON (paste or link)
- Feature flag snapshot
- Routing policy snapshot/version

B) Evidence archive
- Screenshots (links)
- Exported graphs (links)
- Log bundles (links)

C) Glossary (optional)
- DEGRADED: …
- FAILOVER_CANDIDATE: …
- HOLD-DOWN TIMER: …

---

Template change log
- 2025-03-18: initial template created (Tomáš)
- 2025-05-07: added explicit “stop conditions” + “alert inventory” sections; clarified timeline durations (Tomáš, Aisha, Sergio)

Notes to future authors
- Keep the timeline factual and evidence-backed; put interpretation in later sections.
- If this is production, write impact in a way that could be shared internally with Support/CS (avoid speculation, keep it crisp).
- If you discover a security/privacy issue while reviewing logs, stop and escalate to Security & Compliance per policy.
